decision_clause: Ruled out: "keep the wildcard census and rely on the focused-lane guard" — because "the guard catches deletion only, and the review demonstrated growth passing 230/230 with an unreviewed product file present". Scope: packages/schema/src/capability.ts, packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs. Lifecycle: active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree. No file was added, removed, or edited anywhere, including the two scope files that hold the census and the guard. packages/schema/src/capability.ts still returns a single flat record shape from validateCapabilityMatrix — `{ ok: boolean; errors: string[]; rows: CapabilityRow[]; required_event_groups: string[]; coverage: ... }` (capability.ts:49-56), with the failure returns at capability.ts:268 and :271 spreading an `empty` object that still types `rows` as `CapabilityRow[]`, and the tail return at capability.ts:432 computing `ok` from `errors.length === 0`. So the task's contract change is absent as well. On the enforcement side, the coverage machinery in the recorded scope is unchanged and is not a wildcard: tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35 pins the validator's census by a fully enumerated literal path list plus exact counts (`ticket_owned_code_files=64`, `product_code_files=0`, `product_code_paths=none`, terminated by `$`), and tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:476-496 re-derives that same path set from ticket declarations and asserts deep equality against the validator's reported set. scripts/validate-planning.mjs:835-848 admits product source only where a ticket claims it by exact path and fails closed on anything else. The per-lane count guard (tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:717-755, `capability` pinned at 19 cases) is still present but is not the only check standing between a new source file and a green run.
rationale: The ruled-out approach is a positive arrangement: let a wildcard-style census stand as the admission mechanism and treat the focused-lane count guard as sufficient cover for it. Two things keep this tree outside that. First, the tree introduces nothing at all — the diff is empty, so no product or test file enters any census unreviewed, and the concrete failure the decision names (growth passing while an unreviewed product file is present) has no instance here; there is no growth. Second, within the recorded scope the census is not wildcard-shaped and was not made so: tests/planning-contract.test.mjs pins the whole ticket-owned path list verbatim with an exact file count, and tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs binds that pin to an independent re-derivation from the ticket catalog, so an added file breaks both regardless of what the focused-lane counts do. The focused-lane guard is therefore not being relied on alone. I considered the opposite reading — that because the ruled-out approach is phrased as a preservation ("keep"), a tree that changes nothing thereby keeps it. I do not think that carries: the decision rules out a choice made while landing a change, and no change was made, so no such choice is expressed in the tree. That the implementation also failed to deliver the task (the ok:true/ok:false discriminated result contract is simply not there) is a separate defect from the one I was asked about, and failing an obligation to tighten something is not the same as implementing the approach that was ruled out. I mark confidence medium rather than high because the decision's vocabulary ("wildcard census") appears nowhere in the tree — the string "wildcard" has zero occurrences repo-wide — so I am matching it to the census machinery by behavior rather than by name; under any of the candidate referents I could locate, however, the tree is unchanged from base and no ruled-out mechanism is introduced. Approving this empty patch would require re-explaining nothing about the decision, since it touches neither the census nor the guard.
